FolderSync's own state (the folder_sync_seen:<file> marks, folder_sync_enabled) is device-local.

claims.claim: 4. The device id is a setting: it is stored in the same chronicle_settings Preferences DataStore under key device_id, generated on first launch, and kept local. It is not in the sync payload and not in Room. It does not survive a restore, because allowBackup=false, the extraction rules exclude sharedpref/file/database/root, and a corrupt settings file is replaced with empty prefs (new sync identity). Import and sync do not carry it either.

A corrupt settings file is replaced with empty preferences, so the PIN and lock are lost, the device_id is regenerated (new sync identity), and every peer file is re-read once.

DAY_START_MINUTES_KEY is declared in CoreDataModule. The KDoc says it is written by SettingsRepository, but the writer is DayBoundaryRepository (line 41). It is unset by default (midnight) and is not in SettingsRepository.Keys.
Two meanings packed into one field: the app-lock state is three keys (enabled, grace, and pin hash presence as pinSet). Clearing the PIN with no device credential also forces app_lock_enabled=false.

The folder-sync enabled flag, last-sync time and backup folder URI are device-local settings. Only the Room entities cross devices, and the file name embeds the device id (chronicle-sync-<deviceId>.json), so a regenerated device_id leaves the old device's file in the folder as a stale peer.
The settings store has no sync merge stamps. Conflict resolution (updatedAt, deviceId field stamps, tombstones) applies only to entities, so a settings conflict cannot occur.
